product: Resilia (oil of oregano DTC supplement — full-funnel case study)
hook: "12 Facebook Pages Funnel All Their Traffic to ONE Advertorial (4M+ Visits/Mo)" — scale intrigue.
body: 5,900 active Meta ads across 12+ persona pages ("Nutritionist - Allison Langford, PhD" 495 ads, "Dr. Anna Reyes" 634, "Nutravive," "TryResilia," etc.); 544 new creatives/30d; 4.1M monthly visits; 30–50% of traffic to one 7-min parasite advertorial; 6-step video script (symptom → hidden cause → why others failed → mechanism → product → urgency); AI-avatar production; OTO $30→$83; platform-split angles (Meta = gut, YouTube = weight loss).
cta: "Join Funnel of the Week" / comment "RESILIA" (membership pitch).
idea: Persona pages are the distribution infrastructure for belief — 12 authority doors (Schwartz's "same desire, different doors") feed one advertorial; payoffs are risk-splitting, creative flexibility, and scale without saturation.
formatting: Very long text post; hand-graded VALUE competitor-intel.
why_it_works: Each persona is a different trusted voice for the same funnel — the reader who distrusts a brand page may trust a "doctor," and the advertorial does the converting both send to.
what_to_steal: LC's persona-door system: 2–3 honest persona angles (dermatologist-style educator, "waterproof girl" lifestyle, review-style tester) feeding one education article — same desire, different doors.

product: commentary — no product (an agency whitelisting case study; brand unnamed)
hook: "1M+ followers. Still stuck with a $32 AOV." — paradox opener.
body: Case study: a 1M-follower brand stuck at $32 AOV hit $44.83 AOV, +289% revenue, $10K–$20K/day profitable Meta spend, $1M+ months in 60 days — without changing the product or prices; the lever was a creator whitelisting program (first test 3x ROAS/70+ conversions, scaled to 6.1x ROAS); "the biggest growth lever wasn't hidden inside Ads Manager... it was sitting outside the brand."
idea: Whitelisting is a core growth channel, not an experiment — running ads through creators' accounts lifted AOV 40% and revenue 289% for an audience-rich but stuck brand.
sequencing: The thesis (lever sits outside the brand)
formatting: Short-line vertical text post; stat-stack case study.
why_it_works: The "didn't change the product or prices" twist makes whitelisting the sole hero — it isolates the variable, so the reader credits the channel, not the offer.
what_to_steal: LC's whitelisting program as a core channel: run LC's winners through creators' accounts (not just @louisecarter) — the AOV/revenue lift came from the sender, not the creative.

hook: "media buyers everywhere ecstatic they can now lower their Meta CAC by whitelisting Charli XCX UGC ads" — absurdist industry joke.
body: One line: the joke is that media buyers fantasize about whitelisting a pop star's UGC to cut CAC.
idea: None substantive — the joke reveals whitelisting's status as the industry's favorite CAC lever (everyone wishes they had a Charli XCX to whitelist).
sequencing: The joke (whitelist Charli XCX, lower CAC)
The implied premise (whitelisting is the industry's default CAC lever)
The audience signal (13 likes/25 bookmarks — media buyers nodding along)
The meta takeaway (everyone wants a famous face's account to run ads through)
why_it_works: The absurdity (Charli XCX doing UGC) lands because the underlying desire is real — every media buyer wants a famous face's account to run ads through.
what_to_steal: Nothing tactical — the joke confirms whitelisting is the industry's default CAC-reduction fantasy; LC should treat it as table stakes, not a secret.

product: commentary — no product (a CBO structure note)
hook: "I consolidated our whitelisting ads into one ad set with our brand videos." — structure change.
body: Merged whitelisting ads into the brand-video ad set because CBO performs better with fewer ad sets; campaign now = one ad set for statics, one for whitelisting + standard videos; statics kept separate because they "eat the spend... like one big black hole"; min spend limits on the video ad set force even distribution.
idea: Whitelisting ads don't need their own ad set — consolidating them with brand videos under CBO (with min-spend guards against static spend-hogs) simplifies structure without losing performance.
sequencing: The reason (CBO likes fewer ad sets)
The structure (statics ad set / video ad set)
The exception (statics eat spend — kept separate)
The principle (fewer ad sets, controlled distribution)
formatting: Text post + photo; media-buyer build log.
why_it_works: "One big black hole" is a vivid, honest description of static spend behavior — the post earns trust by naming the ugly mechanics, not just the clean structure.
what_to_steal: LC's CBO structure: whitelisted creator ads consolidated with brand videos in one ad set, statics quarantined separately, min-spend limits preventing the black-hole effect.

product: commentary — no product (an agency whitelisting playbook)
hook: "Agencies are getting brands 1,000+ creators for whitelisting ads. The trick is they're pulling from TikTok Shop and moving them to Meta." — playbook reveal.
body: The quiet agency playbook: find the creators driving the most TikTok Shop GMV → request whitelisting rights (not just usage rights) → run the content as ads through the creator's own Meta account; whitelisting rights vs usage rights defined (run ads through their account vs use one piece of content); dark posting = ads that never posted organically; creator incentives: $100 on approval + 3% of ad spend + halo effect (reach beyond their followers); claims 1,000+ creator scale; full walkthrough video linked.
idea: TikTok Shop GMV is the creator-discovery filter for Meta whitelisting — pull proven sellers off TikTok Shop, buy whitelisting rights (not usage), and run their content as dark-posted Meta ads through their accounts.
sequencing: The playbook (find GMV drivers → whitelisting rights → run through their account)
why_it_works: The whitelisting-vs-usage-rights distinction is the genuinely valuable insight — most brands buy the weaker right without knowing the stronger one exists.
what_to_steal: LC's creator pipeline: filter TikTok Shop jewelry sellers by GMV, offer $100 + 3% of spend for whitelisting rights, run their content as dark-posted Meta ads through their accounts.

product: commentary — no product (an incremental-attribution test log)
hook: "Here's how I tested incremental attribution (and a few other ways you can do it)." — test-log framing.
body: Duplicated top-3 ad sets (standard scaling, creator whitelisting, landing page) into a new highest-volume campaign with incremental attribution; day 2 showed major CPA improvement; caveat: shared ads may steal credit from other campaigns; alternatives: full shift to incremental (cleanest, costs a day of bad performance) or the A/B test tool with compare-attribution-settings for apples-to-apples.
idea: Incremental attribution changes what the whitelisting/landing-page ad sets get credit for — the measurement setting itself is a variable worth testing.
sequencing: The test setup (new campaign, top-3 ad sets, incremental)
why_it_works: Honest about the confound (shared ads) instead of just posting the win — the caveat is what makes the test credible.
what_to_steal: Test incremental attribution on LC's whitelisting ad sets before trusting their ROAS — creator-run ads are exactly the kind that over-claim under last-click.

product: commentary — no product (a 7-fig vs 8-fig strategy comparison)
hook: "Our top performing brands have different strategies and focuses depending on their current revenue levels:" — stage-based taxonomy.
body: 7-figure brands: statics-heavy, frequent offer testing, high ad volume, 30–40% UGC/video, Meta + Google only. 8-figure brands: 70%+ partnership ads, monthly product launches, proven offer + known angles, volume focused on whitelisting/video, ~20% statics, Meta + Google ~80% with YouTube rising.
idea: Partnership/whitelisting ads are the 8-figure unlock — 70%+ of creative shifts to partnership ads once a brand has a proven offer and known angles.
why_it_works: The 70%+ partnership-ads stat gives 8-figure brands a concrete creative-mix target — it turns "do more whitelisting" into a budget allocation.
what_to_steal: LC's creative-mix target: with a proven offer, push toward majority partnership/whitelisted video — LC at $25M+ gross is in the 8-figure playbook.

product: commentary — no product (a full growth-system essay)
hook: "growth is not a slope you climb by doing more of the same thing harder. it's a staircase, and every step has a different constraint sitting on it." — thesis opener.
body: Long essay: point-of-constraint scaling; product criteria (high TAM, emotional pain, multiple avatars); margin math (5x markup, 3:1 LTV:CAC); cost hierarchy per funnel step (CPV → CPC → CPLP → CPATC → CPIC → CPP); fix the leak before scaling; creative engines (image = machine gun 3–5/day, video = sniper 5/week); hit rate as a cost lever; the whitelist-persona-pages section: "cheapest scaling move in the whole system... just change who's saying it — take a winning creative and run the exact same thing from a different persona page"; hiring order; direct-factory sourcing.
idea: "Change who's saying it" is the cheapest scaling move — the same winning creative run from a different persona page reaches untouched audience pockets, quietly multiplying one winner into three or four.
sequencing: The two creative engines (machine gun vs sniper)
formatting: Very long text post; essay/manual style.
why_it_works: "People buy from people who look like their world" — the persona-page move works on identity matching, and framing it as the CHEAPEST scaling move makes it the obvious next test.
what_to_steal: LC's persona-page multiplier: every LC winner gets re-run from 3–4 different persona/creator pages (same creative, different sender) — "change who's saying it" before making new creative.

product: commentary — no product (a whitelisting-ops note; brand mentioned: Obvi)
hook: "Creator whitelisting is still the cheapest CAC on Meta. Most lean brands won't touch it." — paradox.
body: The paradox: whitelisting is the cheapest CAC but lean brands avoid it — "not because it doesn't work. Because the ops are miserable." The poster rebuilt Obvi's entire whitelisting pipeline with Perplexity Computer (#PerplexityPartner).
idea: Whitelisting's barrier is operational, not strategic — the cheapest CAC channel goes unused because the pipeline (permissions, accounts, posting) is miserable to run manually.
sequencing: The fix (rebuilt Obvi's pipeline with AI computer)
The sponsored tag (#PerplexityPartner — the pipeline pitch is itself an ad)
why_it_works: "The ops are miserable" names the true objection — it reframes whitelisting adoption from a strategy question into a tooling question.
what_to_steal: LC should attack whitelisting ops first (permissions workflow, account management, posting automation) — the CAC prize is already proven; the unlock is operational.

product: commentary — no product (a Dose Daily competitive x-ray + MCP prompt)
hook: "$12.3M raised. Close to $1 billion valuation. 5 awareness levels. 12 distinct avatars. Dose Daily is pushing some serious volume with their ads." — scale + sophistication flex.
body: A full-census competitive x-ray prompt for GetHookd MCP: find EVERY advertiser on a domain (bare-domain search catches persona/creator/affiliate pages, not just the brand page); paginate to a full census; report scale first (total active ads, coverage %, longest runner); structural breakdown (account split, format mix, TOF/MOF/BOF funnel split by landing destination, SKU split, launch cadence, CTA/lander variants); cluster into micro-angles by hook; diversity axes; gaps; scale math; honesty rules (never invent spend, state coverage).
idea: Persona pages are found by domain-census, not brand search — searching the bare domain reveals the whole shadow network (brand, product-line, persona, creator, affiliate accounts) that brand-name search misses.
formatting: Very long text post + 49s video; prompt-share with 120 bookmarks.
why_it_works: The bare-domain search trick is the genuinely novel method — it exposes the persona-page networks that are invisible to normal ad-library browsing.
what_to_steal: LC's competitor intel: run the bare-domain census on jewelry competitors (Atolea, Mejuri) to map their persona/creator page networks — "expect a brand page, product-line pages, publisher/persona pages, and creator or affiliate accounts."

product: commentary — no product (a partnership-ads vs whitelisting take)
hook: "'Ill just whitelist' — Whitelisting is fine. But meta is REWARDING accounts that commit to partnership ads." — contrarian platform take.
body: Claims first-hand results: lower CPMs, higher CTRs, better CACs from true partnership ads vs plain whitelisting; theorizes Meta has "a finger on the scale" — product teams with adoption KPIs reward the behavior they want; advises running the test.
idea: Partnership ads (the formal Meta format) may outperform raw whitelisting because the platform rewards adoption — "true partnership ads are outperforming everywhere rn."
sequencing: The contrarian claim (Meta rewards partnership ads)
The evidence (lower CPMs, higher CTR, better CAC — first-hand)
The theory (finger on the scale, adoption KPIs)
why_it_works: "Tin foil hat theory" framing makes a platform-favoritism claim feel honest rather than conspiratorial — and first-hand numbers beat theory.
what_to_steal: LC should test formal partnership ads against raw whitelisting head-to-head — if Meta really rewards the format, LC wants the favored version.

product: commentary — no product (a geo category scan: Colibri Skincare dark-spot ads)
hook: "Germany has 85 active German-language ads on Pigmentflecken running 30+ days. The US has 815 on dark spots at 100+." — geo-arbitrage numbers.
body: Category scan: Colibri Skincare owns US dark spots (223 ads, one video at 639K EU reach, Dermatest seal, 60-day guarantee, "a tenth of the competition"); notes "derm persona pages" as a trust device; includes a paste-into-Claude GetHookd MCP prompt for country scanning (market snapshot, burned angles, open angles, localization notes, go/no-go).
idea: "Derm persona pages" are a named trust device in skincare — persona pages + third-party seals (Dermatest) + guarantees are the credibility stack.
sequencing: The trust devices (Dermatest, Made in Germany, 60-day MBG, derm persona pages)
why_it_works: The "a tenth of the competition" line quantifies the moat — owning a category with 10x fewer competitors than the term's total is the whole game.
what_to_steal: LC's credibility stack: persona pages + third-party proof (reviews, press) + guarantee — and the country-scan prompt for jewelry expansion markets.

product: commentary — no product (a persona-page network exposé + Monday-brief prompt)
hook: "A supplement page called The Vitality Edit launched 130 new ads in the last 7 days." — velocity shock.
body: Exposes a persona-page network: The Vitality Edit (200 active, 130 new/7d), The Honest Health (428 active, 61 new), The Antioxidant Edit (183, 44 new), Grounded And Grateful, InStrength, Health That Fits Your Life — "all persona pages, all video-heavy"; the tell: The Vitality Edit and The Honest Health send traffic to the same URL — "Different page names, same brand. That's the persona-page playbook." Includes a Monday competitor-brief MCP prompt (new ads, what's new, kill signals, cross-brand moves, one weekly action).
idea: "Different page names, same brand" is the persona-page tell — multiple editorial-sounding pages funneling to one domain is the playbook, and launch velocity (130 ads/7d) is the detection signal.
sequencing: The network table (6 pages, actives, new, media mix)
formatting: Text post + photo; exposé + prompt share (90 likes, 95 bookmarks).
why_it_works: The side-by-side table makes the network undeniable — and "nobody checking the ad library by hand catches that" sells the automated brief as the only way to see it.
what_to_steal: LC's persona-page network design: 3–4 editorial-named pages (not fake doctors — honest angles like "The Waterproof Edit") funneling to LC, plus the Monday velocity-brief habit to watch competitors doing the same.

product: commentary — no product (a "Barbara Collins" persona-page case + tech-stack prompt)
hook: "The top one runs as a persona page, 'Barbara Collins': 1,058 active ads, menopause skin-fold rash, 90-day guarantee, /intertrigo/adv03 lander. 179 days." — full specimen in one line.
body: Case: a persona page named "Barbara Collins" runs 1,058 active ads for a menopause skin-fold rash offer (90-day guarantee, condition-folder advertorial lander /intertrigo/adv03), live 179 days; avatar = menopausal women, "too embarrassed to bring up"; hook: "Comfortable skin is at the top of my New Year's resolutions" (still live in September); includes a tech-stack reverse-engineering MCP prompt (find the consensus tools on long-running landers: subscription > upsell > quiz > reviews > tracking).
idea: A single persona page can carry 1,058 active ads for 179 days — the persona (a named woman) + embarrassing-condition avatar + condition-folder advertorial is a complete, durable system.
sequencing: The hook (New Year's resolutions, still live)
formatting: Text post + photo; case + prompt share.
why_it_works: 1,058 ads from ONE persona page is the proof of the format's scale ceiling — and the "too embarrassed to bring up" avatar insight shows why the persona (a peer, not a brand) is load-bearing.
what_to_steal: LC's peer-persona page: a named-woman page ("Maya's Waterproof Diaries") running LC's education angles — peer trust for the "my jewelry turns green and I'm embarrassed" avatar.

product: commentary — no product (a hair-thinning persona-page roundup + detection prompt)
hook: "Hair thinning, 180+ days: persona page" — category + endurance + format.
body: Roundup of 180+ day hair-thinning advertisers: The Consumer Pulse (persona page, 199 ads, AI-animated shampoo bottle in shower, "Watch what happens," 183d, 12 DHT herbs, 90-day MBG); Hair Science (Amazon-attribution lander, 301d); BodyWise UGC "don't put this on your face" (309d); Root'd pool side-by-side test vs "scam fibers" (215d); Vedix USA long-hair UGC + quiz (190d); includes a persona-page detection MCP prompt (flag PERSONA when page name is a person/magazine/pulse/edit/community and lander is a different brand; flag Amazon-attribution landers; tag video formats; transcribe top 5).
idea: Persona-page detection is a rule (page name ≠ lander brand) — and the 180+ day survivors show the format mix that endures: AI animation, side-by-side tests, contrarian UGC, quiz funnels.
sequencing: The 5 specimens (page | format | lander | proof | days)
The detection prompt (PERSONA rule, Amazon check, format tags)
The prompt's deliverable E (one persona-page name, one AI-animation concept, one side-by-side test for my product)
formatting: Text post + photo; roundup + prompt share.
why_it_works: The PERSONA detection rule (name-brand mismatch) is a portable heuristic — it turns persona-page spotting from intuition into a query.
what_to_steal: The detection rule for LC's competitor monitoring (flag jewelry persona pages by name≠lander mismatch) + the enduring format mix: AI animation, side-by-side test, contrarian UGC ("don't put this on your face" → LC's "don't take it off in the shower" flip).

hook: "There are 37 ad formats printing right now." — authority list promise.
body: 10 of 37 verified formats; longest runner was an AI podcast at 280 days; full doc linked with live ad + days active + brand ad count per format.
cta: Doc links ("No comment or follow needed").
idea: Format-list proof infrastructure — no persona-page-specific content.
why_it_works: The days-active proof column, as established in prior folders.

product: commentary — no product (a GetHookd MCP workflow post)
hook: "Opened Claude, connected the Gethookd MCP, and asked it to pull every native static hitting a 98-100 performance score in the supplement category." — workflow flex.
body: One search surfaced a blood-pressure brand on 496 active ads, a cat-furniture brand on 961, and "a castor oil persona page pushing 140"; the workflow: filter by days active, group winners by angle/hook/awareness, spit out 30 briefs for the editor next morning — "No swipe folders. No screenshots. Just a live board feeding straight into the brief."
idea: The live-board-to-brief pipeline — MCP-fed ad data grouped by angle/hook/awareness becomes 30 editor briefs overnight, replacing swipe folders entirely.
why_it_works: "No swipe folders. No screenshots" kills the old research ritual — the live board is always current, so briefs are built on what's printing NOW.
what_to_steal: LC's brief pipeline: nightly GetHookd pulls on jewelry terms → group by angle/hook/awareness → morning briefs; and note the "castor oil persona page pushing 140" — persona pages are everywhere, including adjacent verticals.

product: Noverly (an ED supplement brand — a copy teardown of its persona-page funnel)
hook: "Noverly's copy is built around one idea: ED isn't age or testosterone, it's a clogged pipe" — mechanism reframe.
body: Copy teardown: the buyer thinks it's age/stress; the copy hands him a new reason nothing worked ("two arteries measuring barely one to two millimetres"; L-citrulline and beet powder "just ask more dilation from a pipe that has no room to open"); the ads run from persona pages, not the brand; wives leave reviews because husbands "would rather die than type this"; the offer button: "CLEAR THE PIPE NOW."
idea: The persona page + mechanism reframe + bylined authority combo — a doctor-bylined listicle from a persona page (not the brand) gives the buyer a new causal story, and the CTA names the mechanism ("CLEAR THE PIPE NOW").
sequencing: The dismissal of alternatives (dilation with no room)
why_it_works: "Would rather die than type this" shows why the persona page matters — for embarrassing problems, a peer/doctor voice converts where a brand page can't; the single-idea discipline keeps the whole funnel coherent.
what_to_steal: LC's single-idea discipline + persona vehicle: one mechanism ("it's not your skin, it's the plating"), delivered from an educator persona page, CTA naming the mechanism ("GO WATERPROOF").

product: commentary — no product (a Prime Prometics micro-angle x-ray + MCP prompt)
hook: "Prime Prometics has 2,828 active ads. Distinct avatars: 24 — all women, ages 40 to 65+." — scale + avatar depth.
body: X-ray: 2,828 active ads, 24 distinct avatars (6 life-event: mother of the bride, reunion, divorcee, first date, local-news clip, church community), ~28 narrator personas across 11 persona types run through 15 pages — "creative diversity at its best"; includes a full micro-angle x-ray MCP prompt (find library, report scale, read transcripts not copy, cluster by buyer-motivation micro-angle, diversity axes, gaps, scale math).
idea: The scale math: micro-angles × narrator personas × pages = thousands of ads on ONE product — 24 avatars × 28 narrators × 15 pages is how a single SKU sustains 2,828 active ads.
sequencing: The verdict (creative diversity at its best)
why_it_works: The life-event avatars (mother of the bride, reunion, divorcee) show the granularity that sustains scale — each life event is its own emotional entry point, which is why one product needs 24 avatars.
what_to_steal: LC's avatar × narrator matrix: jewelry life-event avatars (wedding, vacation, gym, first date, reunion) × narrator personas × pages — run the same multiplication on LC's hero pieces; and the "read the transcripts, not the copy" x-ray rule.
